name: Prince Arthas
aliases: Your Highness (Jaina, as a joke; Sylvanas, formal)

physicalDetails.detail: Chapter 6 (first on-page appearance, seen by Jaina): comes between the tents at a long stride, helmet in one hand; hair dark with sweat at the temples and gold everywhere else; broader than she remembers, 'a man now', a hammer at his belt instead of a practice sword. Armour polished by someone else (the crest of Lordaeron on the breastplate), greaves plastered brown with camp mud from the knee down. Gloved; wears gauntlets (one closes on Jaina's dead right arm). Puts the helmet on again at the top of the lane before going to meet a rider.

voiceMarkers.detail: Warm, quick, easy, laughs out loud. First line: 'Jaina! Light's sake. Jaina Proudmoore, on my hill. Did Antonidas finally throw you out?' Teases ('I always listen to you all the way to the end. It's the only way to get a word in afterwards.'). Courteous and exact to Sylvanas ('Ranger-General. You're a long way from home.'). Dry about Barov ('Good. He'd sue me for the rest of it, and he'd talk for an hour first.'). On Jaina's case: 'Jaina. I don't doubt you.' Then the turn: 'Yes. I am.' Gentle, concrete, personal about the orc war ('That's the Garrow farm. Old Garrow, his daughter, her two boys. I ate supper at their table on the way up here; the boys wanted to hold my hammer. Yesterday I helped carry them out... I can see that from my tent door. I can't see your grain.'). 'I believe you.' Gives practical next steps ('write it down... I'll send it to my father tonight with my own rider'), and kindness ('Get something to eat before you go; you look like you haven't eaten since Dalaran.'). Orders to the staff by event ('See they're fed, and the horses watered.').

beliefs.belief: The orc war is the real, visible threat: bands 'out of the camps', with axes, who know the hills better than his scouts; every farm between Strahnbrad and the river is waiting to be next, and men in his camp have families on those farms.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: The farm dead are real (the Garrow farm burned; he helped carry out the bodies). His priority is understandable and wrong for this threat.

beliefs.belief: The plague warning is credible but can wait: he believes Jaina, sends her to write it out for his father and the council, and will come to Andorhal once the hills are quiet.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Will be shown to be too late; the plague is already in the granaries.

beliefs.belief: (Seen through Jaina's memory) The orc internment camps are necessary; orcs are beasts and the fences are why. He held this before the fence and after seeing the female and infant.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Held with the same sureness by his own account of that night. Jaina leaves the question of fairness open ('Perhaps the fences had been the right answer all along') and answers 'No' about his reading of it today.

goalsAtChapterEnd.active: Finish the war in the Strahnbrad hills; send Jaina's warning to King Terenas tonight by his own rider; reach Andorhal when the hills are quiet.
goalsAtChapterEnd.underlying: Protect the people he can see and name; be the commander who wins the war in front of him. (Read from outside.)

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd.state: Warm, sure, and short of time: laughs at seeing Jaina, then sobers; sorry ('I'm sorry. I am.') but does not change course; leaves at a rider's arrival with the officers closing round him. Not cruel and not blind to Jaina; he cannot see the poison.

decisionsThisChapter.detail: Heard Jaina's warning fully, with arms folded and his weight set, the way Jaina has seen him listen to a fencing master; looked at the sheet, put one gloved finger on the knife slit ('That's us.') and drew a Barov slip half out to read the seal; left the sheet in her hand; said 'I don't doubt you.'
Studied Sylvanas long and steady when she called his decision, and confirmed it ('Yes. I am.').

Turned Jaina to face the valley and named the burning Garrow farm as the reason; chose the orcs. Told her to write it all down; promised a rider to his father that night and a visit to Andorhal when the hills were quiet; ordered the party fed and watered; left to meet a rider from the east at a canter.

abilitiesDemonstrated.ability: Commands a large camp: officers close round him at once; a boy runs messages; riders go out from his tent east and return; he answers a field rider immediately.

Reads a person quickly: sees Jaina's injuries as soon as he is close enough ('What happened to your hands?'); answers her emotionally and personally; has a ready, warm manner with strangers (sergeant, officers, Sylvanas).

howOthersAddressHim.speaker: Sylvanas (aloud, chapter 6)
howOthersAddressHim.pattern: 'Your Highness', the two words perfectly level.

howOthersAddressHim.speaker: Jaina (aloud, chapter 6)
howOthersAddressHim.pattern: 'Arthas' when asking him to listen; 'Your Highness' once as a joke at first sight. Narration: 'Arthas'.

howOthersAddressHim.speaker: Camp sergeant (chapter 6)
howOthersAddressHim.pattern: 'Everybody knows him, miss.' (no title in the line).

howHeAddressesOthers.pattern: 'Jaina' warmly and often; 'Jaina Proudmoore, on my hill' (full name once, for show); 'Jaina. I don't doubt you.' He does not say 'Proudmoore' (that is Sylvanas).
'Ranger-General', with a small correct bow from the neck, twice.

bodyLanguagePatterns.detail: Chapter 6: stops in mud and laughs out loud; comes on with officers hurrying to keep up; carries his helmet; folds his arms and sets his weight to listen, face serious; bends to look at the sheet, hair falling over his brow; puts one gloved finger on the knife slit; draws out a slip with the same finger; looks past Jaina's shoulder at the far hills and the smoke whenever she presses; studies Sylvanas 'long and steady' and does not snap; puts a hand on Jaina's shoulder and turns her to the valley; squeezes her (dead) right arm; gives Sylvanas a second small bow from the neck; turns his head to an officer to give the order for food; goes up the lane toward a rider, helmet in hand, then puts it on.

knowledge.detail: REFERENCED ONLY. Road talk: he has his army up at Strahnbrad, burning out orcs from the camps who are burning farms in the hills; the army has taken remounts and oats at the King's price; soldiers on every road that way; a company of King's foot cut across for the hill road and the prince, and do not pay (toll-keeper). Sylvanas: 'If he had an opinion about grain at all, it would be somewhere below the orcs, and below his horse.'

Chapter 6: knows Jaina (old friendship; calls her by first name; knows she studies with Antonidas). Knows the Barovs as a court house with granaries (Lord Barov would 'sue me... and talk for an hour first'). Hears and understands the plague warning: flour as carrier, a made thing, bread, Millhaven's dead walking north, a village south saved by burning flour, depot slips, Andorhal at one end of every slip. Does not take or read the sheet beyond the knife slit and a Barov seal. Is told Andorhal's granaries should be shut and does not shut them. Knows the Garrow farm has burned and the band came out of the camps.

arc.currentPosition: Chapter 6: on the page. A warm, capable commander who believes Jaina and does not act on it; his courtesy and his reasons are real. He walks into the next rider with Jaina's paper never taken. Sylvanas has judged him: a good commander with the wrong war for this.
